articles.title: Brother didn't match description of 'Putney pusher', suspect's sisters tell BBC
articles.summary: Speaking on BBC Radio 4's Today programme, Nicholas Brandram's sisters accused the Metropolitan Police of being "negligent and reckless".
articles.body:
The sisters of the man suspected of being the so-called "Putney pusher" have told the BBC their brother was innocent, and the police showed "no urgency" to clear his name.

Speaking on BBC Radio 4's Today programme, Nicholas Brandram's sisters accused the Metropolitan Police of being "negligent and reckless".

Brandram was found dead on Tuesday evening and his family said he "took his own life after months of immense pressure" caused by the investigation.

Brandram's sisters Alexia Hicks and Sophie Voelcker told Today presenter Justin Webb their brother's mental health deteriorated after his arrest and questioned why the police were not able to carry out DNA tests that could have proved his innocence.

articles.title: The best heating pads to relieve aches and cramps, according to physical therapists
articles.summary: Heating pads can help to treat aches, soreness and pains in your muscles and joints. I rounded up the best heating pads recommended by experts from brands like Homedics, Bearaby, Sunbeam and more.
articles.body: As a gym-goer and former high school athlete, I’m no stranger to aches and pains. Thankfully, heating pads are a safe and easy way to soothe soreness at home. Specifically, according to the experts, heating pads reduce your body’s perception of pain and stiffness by generating heat to increase blood flow to a certain area, which helps to increase mobility and circulation, reduce inflammation, and help you feel more relaxed. That being said, I gathered a list of expert-recommended and editor-tested heating pads to consider for treating muscle aches, menstrual cramps and more. You can find that list below along with guidance and shopping tips from Dr. Michele Christian, a physical therapist at Stroma Physical Therapy in New York City, Dr. Rolland Miro, a sports therapist, chiropractor and the owner/director of Manhattan Sports Therapy in New York, and Dr. Karena Wu, a board-certified clinical specialist in orthopedic physical therapy and owner and clinical director of ActiveCare Physical Therapy in NYC. Want more from NBC Selected? Sign up for our newsletter, The Selection, and shop smarter. The best heating pads Best overall NBC Selected senior editor Nikki Brown has had this heating pad for years and still uses it monthly when she has menstrual cramps. It’s made from a machine-washable, velveteen fabric pad and has four heat settings available on the included single-button controller. “It heats up fast and has an auto shutoff feature that comes in handy when using overnight,” says Brown. The pad also has moist heating features; to use, the brand says you should lightly mist the surface of your pad with water, or pat it gently with a wet sponge to add moisture. Best electric heating pad This electric option comes recommended by Chattanooga, who says it doesn’t need water to provide moist heat. The pad, which uses a flannel covering to draw moisture from the air, also includes a digital controller that lets you program and monitor the temperature and duration of your heating treatment up to 30 minutes, according to the brand. The temperature can be controlled between 88 and 166 degrees Fahrenheit, and it has a lockout mode that protects against accidental or inconsistent setting changes during the treatment. Best microwaveable heating pad This microwaveable option comes recommended by Christian because of its cordless design and washable, cotton covering. Christian also says it can be dampened with water before microwaving to provide moist heat, and that it gradually loses heat while in use, which reduces your risk of burns. The pad’s star-shaped design provides more targeted and even heating, and the millet, flaxseed and claybead filling makes it flexible enough to be used on any part of the body, according to UNCN. You can also use it as a cold compress — just stick it in the fridge or freezer to cool it down. Best budget heating pad This moist heating pad “gets very hot and maintains heat well,” says Miro. To use it, the brand recommends heating the compress to your desired temperature using a hydroculator or, for those of you using it at home, a heated pot of water, or a microwave as a last resort. Since it gets so hot, Miro recommends layering a towel or other comfortable buffer between your skin and the pad, which he does in his own practice: “We wrap these up in a towel and place a few folded towels on the person before placing this pack on them,” he says. This pad is also pliable and more flexible when it’s heated, making it easier to mold to the shape of your targeted area, according to the brand. Best splurge This heating pad from Bearaby (who also makes the NBC Selected Wellness Award-winning Terraclay Dreamer Sleep Mask), is both warmable and freezable, making it a versatile option for anyone in need of a dual heating pad/cold compress. Former NBC Selected editorial projects manager Rebecca Rodriguez calls it a “lifesaver” when she’s suffering from cramps, and says the weighted design gives her “the feeling of a big hug when [she] really needs one.” She also says that it stays warm the longest out of any heating pads she’s tried — after microwaving, it can stay hot for up to a full hour, according to the brand. This pad is also machine-washable. Best large heating pad Wu recommends Sunbeam’s heating pads because they’re easy to use and budget-friendly. This model comes with a nine-foot cord, a two-hour auto shut off, and a slide-button controller with three heat settings, according to the brand. It’s also great for targeting larger areas — it has a 24-inch length that Wu says is big enough to work “pretty much everywhere you need it on the body.” It also has a machine-washable cover, and can be used with moist heat by lightly spraying the surface with water. Best for back pain If you want to target your back or waist areas, Wu suggests this microwaveable heating pad from Suzzipad. It has an ergonomic design that fits around your lower waist to better localize your heat therapy session, according to the brand. It’s filled with flaxseed, millet, clay beads and sorghum, which can trap both heat and cold, making it a great dual treatment option. The pad is also double-sided, with one side made of a soft, fuzzy material and the other side made of a smooth, Dutch velvet for extra heat retention, according to the brand. Best for travel NBC Selected editorial operations associate Jem Alabi usually opts for the traditional heated rubber water bottle, but when it comes to travel, she says it’s not feasible outside of the home. “This pad has been a miracle for me many times,” she says. She uses it not only for aches and pains, but to help with creating and preserving heat in cold airports and on planes. The pad gives up to two hours of heat on a full charge, and she loves how it’s designed to be easily portable. “You can literally walk around or sit for hours without needing your hands, and it’s small and not really noticeable under clothing,” she says. How I picked the best heating pads While pulling together this list, experts told me to focus mainly on the different types of heating pads. Types: According to Wu, the two main categories of heating pads are moist pads and dry pads. Moist pads, often used by professionals in clinical settings, are wet and require a heating pad protector and layers of material between the skin and pad. “Moist heat is the optimal choice,” says Miro, “but many require a special device to heat it called a hydrocollator.” Although hydrocollators are often used in chiropractic and physical therapy offices, Miro says that you can substitute at home by bringing a pot of hot water up to temperature and submerging your pad instead. Dry heating pads, like electric and microwaveable, are more common. Electric pads plug into a wall socket and usually have adjustable heat settings, whereas the level of warmth from microwaveable pads depends on the amount of heating time. Often filled with natural materials, microwaveable pads, though effective, can be more difficult to temperature-control, says Wu. “It’s not as easy to control the heat because if it’s heated too much, you have to let it sit to cool it down,” she says. Our list includes every type of heating pad mentioned above. How to shop for a heating pad When shopping for a heating pad of your own, experts recommend keeping the following factors in mind. Fit/size: “A good heating pad is one that molds well to the desired region,” says Christian. She suggests considering the size of a heating pad before buying to make sure that it’s able to comfortably cover your entire affected area. Wu also says that you should consider how the heating pad will fit/cover your target area with the least amount of external support necessary, meaning that you should choose a heating pad that doesn’t need other items to hold it in place.Settings: Christian says that it’s also important to choose a heating pad with “a variety of temperature options to fit your comfort level.” Heating pads with adjustable temperature settings are great for keeping the pad within your personal heat tolerance, and added settings and features can be useful for preventing burns or accidents. For example, an electric heating pad with an automatic shut off timer can help to improve safety by reducing the risk of prolonged exposure, she says.Material: Choosing the right material for your heating pad can affect your pad’s comfort and heat tolerance levels. According to Wu, natural fibers, such as cotton or linen, are best since they can easily withstand heat, whereas some synthetic fibers will heat up along with the pad. Polyester is also a popular option since it’s non-flammable with a very high melting point, says Christian. For the pad’s fill, Wu also suggests organic materials, such as beans, rice, corn, flaxseed and wheat. articles.title: Terremoto de magnitude 4,8 atinge região metropolitana de Santiago, no Chile | G1
articles.body:
Um terremoto de magnitude 4,8 atingiu na sexta-feira a Região Metropolitana do Chile , onde fica a capital, Santigo , informou o Centro Sismológico Euro-Mediterrâneo (EMSC).

O tremor, ocorrido a uma profundidade de 98 km, teve sua magnitude rebaixada em relação à estimativa inicial de 5,2, segundo o EMSC.

O epicentro do tremor foi a 33 km da capital do país, no conjunto habitacional Vila Presidente Frei.

Não houve registro de mortos, feridos ou danos à infraestrutura até a última atualização desta reportagem. Também não há risco de tsunami, segundo o EMSC.

articles.title: No Dia do Chile, descubra 5 vinhos tintos de excelente custo-benefício | G1
articles.standfirst: Famoso pela Carménère, país andino é referência também em outras uvas.
articles.summary: Famoso pela Carménère, país andino é referência também em outras uvas.
articles.body:
A relação do Chile com a uva Carménère é famosa no mundo inteiro há pelo menos três décadas, ou seja, desde quando análises de laboratório revelaram que as vinhas que, durante cerca de um século se pensava fossem de Merlot, eram na verdade Carménère .

A descoberta projetou o país andino no cenário mundial justamente pela qualidade de seus vinhos de Carménère , uma uva tinta de origem francesa, mas que na França, atualmente, sobrevive apenas em pequenas áreas na região de Bordeaux. Ou seja, se não fosse pelo Chile, hoje estaria extinta ou quase.

Ao mesmo tempo, os viticultores chilenos aprimoraram seu conhecimento sobre outras uvas a começar pela Malbec, a variedade ícone da Argentina , a Pinot Noir e a Cabernet Sauvignon, que hoje é a uva tinta mais plantada do país .

Essas são apenas algumas das principais castas, mas o Chile conta ainda com outras variedades menos exploradas. A centenária vinícola Santa Carolina, por exemplo, resgatou a Romano, uma rara uva tinta francesa praticamente extinta na França .

No Dia do Chile, convidamos você a desbravar uvas icônicas desse país. Conheça a seguir cinco vinhos tintos de excelente custo-benefício para descobrir o melhor da enologia andina.

Santa Carolina El Pacto Acordo nº 5 Romano. — Foto: Porto a Porto/Divulgação.

Vinho elegante elaborado com a rara uva Romano. Seus aromas lembram frutas vermelhas frescas, como framboesa e amora, e frutas escuras, como ameixa e cereja, com nuances de baunilha e toques herbáceos que enriquecem a experiência. Em boca, os taninos são aveludados, com uma ótima estrutura e excelente potencial de envelhecimento.

Amadureceu durante 12 meses em barricas de carvalho e é perfeito com carnes vermelhas, carnes de caça, pato e risotos com carnes.

Estelar 57 Carménère. — Foto: Porto a Porto/Divulgação.

Produzido com a uva icônica do Chile, esse tinto apresenta aromas de frutas vermelhas, como framboesa, e pretas, como cereja. Em boca, destaque para os taninos macios e a boa persistência. Ideal com pizzas, massas ao sugo frango ao curry.

Caliterra Reserva Malbec. — Foto: Porto a Porto/Divulgação.

Um vinho Malbec vibrante e elegante do Vale do Colchagua, com aromas de frutas escuras frescas, como mirtilos e ginja, flores como violetas e sutis notas picantes e herbáceas. Em boca, é fresco e equilibrado, com taninos macios e um final persistente.

50% do vinho amadureceu por 6 meses em barricas de carvalho francês de segundo uso. Acompanha massas com molhos de carnes e pizzas como pepperoni, com carnes e cogumelos.

Tabali Pedregoso Gran Reserva Cabernet Sauvignon. — Foto: Porto a Porto/Divulgação.

Tinto estruturado e saboroso, elaborado com uvas Cabernet Sauvignon colhidas manualmente em vinhedos no Vale do Maipo.

Apresenta aromas de cerejas, violeta e groselha, com toques tostados e defumados. Em boca, é redondo, com taninos sedosos, grande estrutura e abundantes sabores de frutas. Amadureceu 10 meses em barricas de carvalho francês e é perfeito com carnes vermelhas grelhadas e assadas.

Carolina Reserva Pinot Noir. — Foto: Porto a Porto/Divulgação.

Apresenta aromas de frutos vermelhos e notas de alcaçuz. Em boca, destacam-se a acidez delicada, os taninos macios e o final equilibrado. Amadureceu por 6 meses em barrica de carvalho americano e francês. Ideal para acompanhar rosbife ou salada com atum.

articles.title: Jovem é atingido por arpão na cabeça durante pescaria em Rifaina | G1
articles.standfirst: Segundo informação repassada à polícia, o disparo foi acidental e feito por um amigo que pescava com ele. Jovem foi levado à Santa Casa de Franca, teve o arpão retirado e já está em casa.
articles.summary: Equipamento teria sido disparado acidentalmente por um amigo perto da Usina de Jaguara. Objeto atingiu o couro cabeludo e rapaz se recupera em casa.
articles.body:
Um jovem de 22 anos foi atingido na cabeça por um arpão durante uma pesca subaquática no Rio Grande, nas proximidades da Usina de Jaguara, em Rifaina (SP), na tarde de quinta-feira (17). Ele foi socorrido, teve o arpão retirado na Santa Casa de Franca (SP) e já está em casa.

Segundo a EPTV, afiliada da TV Globo, o jovem pescava com um amigo. A informação repassada à polícia é de que o disparo foi acidental e feito pelo amigo, que manuseava o equipamento.

O arpão atingiu o couro cabeludo. De acordo com a EPTV, o objeto não chegou a atingir áreas neurológicas.

Jovem é atingido por arpão durante pescaria em Rifaina, SP — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

O próprio amigo levou o jovem a uma unidade de saúde de Rifaina, onde foi feito um curativo. Em seguida, ele foi levado de ambulância à Santa Casa de Pedregulho (SP) e, depois, transferido para a Santa Casa de Franca.

Em Franca, o jovem passou por exames e teve o arpão retirado pelos médicos. Ele recebeu alta e continua a recuperação em casa, onde precisa manter cuidados com o ferimento.

Em julho de 2023, o mecânico Alexandro Oliveira, de 41 anos, desapareceu no Rio Grande, em Rifaina, enquanto praticava pesca com arpão à noite. O corpo dele foi encontrado cerca de uma semana depois.

articles.title: Processo seletivo Funai Ji-Paraná: vagas com salários até R$ 7,6 mil | G1
articles.standfirst: Inscrições já estão abertas e seguem até 25 de setembro. Seleção será realizada em duas etapas: análise curricular e entrevista.
articles.summary: O processo seletivo Funai Ji-Paraná oferece 59 vagas imediatas e inscrições até 25 de setembro para cargos com remuneração de até R$ 7,6 mil e benefícios.
articles.body:
Processo seletivo - Reprodução — Foto: Prefeitura de Porto Velho

A Fundação Nacional dos Povos Indígenas (Funai) abriu processo seletivo simplificado com 59 vagas imediatas para atuação em Ji-Paraná (RO), além da formação de cadastro reserva. As inscrições já estão abertas e seguem até 25 de setembro. Os salários variam de R$ 2,8 mil a R$ 7,6 mil.

As inscrições são gratuitas e devem ser feitas por meio de formulário eletrônico disponível no site da banca organizadora, o Instituto Avalia.

As oportunidades são para os cargos de agente temporário em proteção territorial, com atuação em ações de proteção, e de especialista temporário em proteção territorial, nas áreas de apoio administrativo, suporte em atividades de campo, geoprocessamento e manejo integrado do fogo.

De acordo com o edital, os contratados vão contar com auxílio-alimentação, auxílio-creche e auxílio pré-escolar. A seleção será realizada em duas etapas: análise curricular e entrevista.

As oportunidades são para cargos de níveis médio e superior, com jornada de 40 horas semanais. Os contratos são temporários e têm duração de até quatro anos.

Confira as vagas, salários e requisitos:

Agente Temporário em Proteção Territorial – Apoio a Ações de Proteção

Vagas: 32 Ampla Concorrência, 1 PcD e 15 Pessoa Preta, Indígena e Quilombola; + CR.

Especialista Temporário em Proteção Territorial – Apoio Administrativo

Vagas: 3 Ampla Concorrência e 1 Pessoa Preta, Indígena e Quilombola; + CR

Escolaridade: nível superior em qualquer área.

Especialista Temporário em Proteção Territorial – Suporte em Atividades de Campo

Vagas: 3 Ampla Concorrência e 1 Pessoa Preta, Indígena e Quilombola + CR

Escolaridade: graduação em Ciências Sociais, Sociologia, Antropologia, Ciência Política, História, Geografia, Ciências Ambientais, Gestão Ambiental, Ciências Biológicas, Engenharia Florestal, Engenharia Ambiental e Sanitária, Engenharia Civil, Agronomia ou Engenharia Agronômica.

Especialista Temporário em Proteção Territorial – Geoprocessamento

Escolaridade: graduação em Geografia, Engenharia de Agrimensura, Engenharia Cartográfica, Engenharia Florestal, Engenharia Ambiental e Sanitária, Agronomia ou Engenharia Agronômica. Também podem concorrer candidatos com graduação em Ciências Sociais, Sociologia, Antropologia, Ciência Política, História, Ciências Ambientais, Gestão Ambiental ou Ciências Biológicas, desde que tenham pós-graduação na área de geoprocessamento.

Especialista Temporário em Proteção Territorial – Manejo Integrado do Fogo

Vagas: 1Ampla Concorrência e 1 Pessoa Preta, Indígena e Quilombola + CR.

O candidato pode consultar o cronograma completo, as atribuições dos cargos e os demais requisitos no edital do processo seletivo.

articles.standfirst: Mulher foi atingida por carreta após se desequilibrar em moto; trânsito ficou bloqueado na Avenida das Torres e congestionamento chegou até a Cidade Nova.
articles.summary: Acidente na Avenida das Torres entre moto e carreta deixa mulher gravemente ferida e causa longo congestionamento em Manaus nesta sexta-feira (18).
articles.body:
Equipes de socorro foram acionadas após um acidente envolvendo uma carreta e uma motocicleta na Avenida das Torres. — Foto: Karla Melo/Rede Amazônica

Uma mulher, cuja identidade ainda não identificada, ficou gravemente ferida em um acidente entre uma moto e uma carreta na Avenida das Torres, em Manaus , nesta sexta-feira (18). Equipes do Serviço de Atendimento Móvel de Urgência (Samu) atenderam a ocorrência. Até a última atualização desta reportagem, não havia informações sobre o estado de saúde da vítima.

Testemunhas disseram à equipe da Rede Amazônica que a carreta passou ao lado da moto, a passageira se desequilibrou e foi atingida. O veículo não parou e já não estava no local quando o socorro chegou.

Parte das três faixas da Avenida das Torres foi interditada para o atendimento. O trânsito ficou congestionado até a região do bairro Cidade Nova.

O condutor da moto, Alexandre, motorista de aplicativo, contou que trafegava devagar quando uma viatura mudou de faixa à sua frente. Ele disse que freou para dar passagem e, em seguida, sentiu a passageira cair sobre ele.

“Eu só senti quando a mulher foi passando para cima de mim, eu não sei se [a carreta] bateu na perna dela, sei que já foi batendo ela e não consegui mais segurar a moto", contou o condutor à Rede Amazônica.

Alexandre teve ferimentos no braço, costas e pé. Ele permaneceu consciente e disse à polícia e ao Samu que procuraria atendimento médico por conta própria.

A passageira recebeu atendimento no local e foi levada de ambulância para uma unidade hospitalar. da capital

articles.title: Assar sem forno elétrico: o que o forno de lenha entrega | G1
articles.standfirst: Forno elétrico é um dos maiores consumidores da casa. Veja o que o forno do fogão a lenha faz diferente e como controlar a temperatura sem termostato
articles.summary: Forno elétrico é um dos maiores consumidores da casa. Veja o que o forno do fogão a lenha faz diferente e como controlar a temperatura sem termostato
articles.body:
Forno elétrico está entre os aparelhos que mais consomem energia numa residência, e ele é usado justamente nos preparos longos — pão, assado, bolo. Quem tem fogão a lenha tem um forno já aquecido pelo mesmo fogo que cozinha. A dificuldade não é a temperatura: é aprender a controlá-la sem termostato.

Fornos de ferro fundido para fogão a lenha, com tampa de ferro e de vidro — Foto: Divulgação / Panela de Ferro Fundido

O forno elétrico trabalha por ciclos : liga a resistência, atinge a temperatura, desliga, cai, liga de novo. O forno de lenha em ferro fundido trabalha por inércia : a massa do metal e da alvenaria guarda calor e o entrega de forma contínua. É por isso que pão e assado longo saem com crosta e cozimento mais uniformes — não há oscilação de resistência ligando e desligando.

Forno elétrico oscila em ciclos; o de lenha entrega calor contínuo por inércia. A diferença aparece na crosta.

Como controlar a temperatura sem termostato

1.Regule o fogo, não o forno: mais lenha e registro aberto sobem a temperatura; registro fechado a segura.

2.U se o t este da mão ou um termômetro de forno para calibrar o seu — cada fogão é diferente.

3.Espere estabilizar antes de colocar o alimento; forno em subida assa desigual.

4.P ara preparo delicado, trabalhe no c alor residual, depois de o fogo baixar.

5.A note o que funcionou: o controle vem da repetição, não de um número universal.

Abrir o forno para conferir derruba a temperatura — daí a vantagem prática do vidro em preparos que exigem acompanhamento, como pão. Os fornos de ferro fundido vêm nas duas versões, em vários tamanhos.

Modelos com tampa de ferro e de vidro: acompanhar o assado sem abrir o forno — Foto: Divulgação / Panela de Ferro Fundido

Sediada em Divinópolis , no Centro-Oeste de Minas, a Panela de Ferro Fundido trabalha com fornos e componentes para fogão a lenha. Os modelos estão no catálogo de fornos de ferro fundido , com entrega para todo o Brasil.

articles.title: Empresa e cidade: quando um empreendimento vira transformação urbana | G1
articles.standfirst: Incorporadoras começam a reconhecer que crescimento genuíno integra responsabilidade com o espaço onde operam.
articles.summary: Incorporadoras começam a reconhecer que crescimento genuíno integra responsabilidade com o espaço onde operam.
articles.body:
Um biombo feito com terra compactada está sendo integrado a um empreendimento imobiliário no Juvevê. A taipa, uma técnica construtiva milenar, reaparece não como estrutura, mas como presença visual que marca a transição entre o espaço público da rua e o ambiente privado do empreendimento. É uma escolha curiosa que levanta questão maior sobre o papel da empresa no espaço urbano que ocupa.

Quando uma incorporadora decide investir em renovação urbana genuína, a ação vai além de adorno. Funciona como estratégia que qualifica o bairro e, consequentemente, agrega valor ao próprio empreendimento. Ruas mais cuidadas, espaços públicos projetados com intenção e infraestrutura pensada com propósito transformam não apenas métricas imobiliárias, mas a vida cotidiana de quem passa por ali.

Imagem noturna da fachada do Tauá. — Foto: Dreamis/Divulgação.

No Juvevê, a escolha da taipa no acesso do Tauá exemplifica essa dinâmica. O Tauá é um empreendimento de duas torres com 58 unidades, lançado em 2025 pela Dreamis Incorporadora .

A incorporadora, que atua há cinco anos no mercado imobiliário de Curitiba com foco em projetos de alto padrão pensados para bem-estar integrado, escolheu trazer a taipa como elemento visual do projeto. Não é estrutura, mas uma obra de arte que se abre para a rua. Simboliza reconhecimento de que o bairro merecia algo além de mais um empreendimento.

Mas essa não é primeira vez que a Dreamis investe em renovação urbana genuína. No Centro Cívico, a empresa revitalizou um prédio histórico do século XIX que servia como extensão do antigo cassino do Ahú. A região, que estava abandonada, tornou-se sede da empresa após a revitalização, transformando também o entorno imediato.

Essas duas escolhas — a taipa no Tauá e a revitalização no Centro Cívico — revelam um padrão deliberado. Não são atos isolados de responsabilidade urbana; são sinais de que a empresa reconhece o impacto que deixa nos lugares onde atua.

A taipa especificamente funciona como símbolo potente. Uma técnica que construiu cidades inteiras ressurge em um contexto contemporâneo, sinalizando que qualidade duradoura é atemporal.

Da mesma forma, a revitalização da Casa Dreamis demonstra o respeito pelo entorno e pela história da região, trazendo de volta um espaço que foi ponto de encontro no bairro e que agora retorna ao seu auge.

Daniel Pizzatto, sócio-fundador e diretor executivo da Dreamis, explica como essas escolhas se alinham: "Quando você atua em um bairro, a pergunta central é: o que fica para o entorno? A revitalização do prédio histórico no Centro Cívico e a escolha da taipa no Tauá respondem essa pergunta da mesma forma: contribuindo para a segurança urbana, trazendo elementos arquitetônicos e artísticos genuínos para o cotidiano do bairro. Essa é a diferença entre investimento transacional e transformação real."

Essa abordagem coloca em foco uma dinâmica frequentemente negligenciada: empresas que apenas extraem valor do bairro deixam um impacto diferente daquelas que investem em transformação genuína. Quem reconhece responsabilidade urbana deixa uma marca distinta no lugar onde atua.

Imagem aérea da Casa Dreamis durante a revitalização, em 2025. — Foto: Juliano Rossetto.

O mercado começa a reconhecer responsabilidade urbana

O movimento não é isolado. Reflete uma tendência maior onde qualidade deixou de ser sinônimo de isolamento de classe.

Empreendimentos que beneficiam o entorno ganham reconhecimento de mercado, valorizam-se melhor, atraem compradores que reconhecem responsabilidade urbana.

articles.title: Psychology says people who feel uncomfortable when someone is too kind to them aren't ungrateful: What makes receiving affection difficult
articles.summary: Someone offers to help you with a difficult task. You immediately say, “No, no, I’ll manage.” A friend compliments you, and you explain why the shirt .
articles.body: Someone offers to help you with a difficult task. You immediately say, “No, no, I’ll manage.” A friend compliments you, and you explain why the shirt was not that good looking. A loved one says, “You can always talk to me,” but you change the subject. Someone gives you a thoughtful gift, and instead of enjoying it, you start wondering what you should give them in return. For some people, receiving kindness is surprisingly uncomfortable.They may care deeply about the people around them. They may be the first to offer help, remember birthdays or check on a friend. Yet when someone does the same for them, they feel awkward, guilty or unsure how to respond. This can be confusing, especially when they genuinely want to be loved and supported.Feeling uncomfortable when someone is kind does not automatically mean a person is ungrateful. Psychology offers several possible explanations, including attachment patterns, self-worth, fear of dependence and past experiences. But there is no single explanation for everyone.When kindness feels like a responsibilityFor some people, kindness can feel less like a gift and more like a responsibility. They may believe that accepting something creates an obligation. If someone gives them time, they must give time back. If someone offers emotional support, they must be equally supportive. This does not necessarily mean they do not appreciate the gesture. They may simply find it difficult to accept care without feeling that they owe something.Research on attachment and relationships has explored how people experience support, closeness and dependence. These patterns can influence whether receiving care feels reassuring or uncomfortable. However, personal experiences also matter. Someone may have grown up in an environment where favours came with expectations. Another person may simply prefer to keep relationships balanced.They may be used to being the independent oneSome people are comfortable handling everything themselves. They solve problems without asking for help. They keep their worries private. They prefer to be the person others can rely on rather than the person who needs support. Over time, independence can become part of their identity. So when someone offers help, their response may be automatic: “I can do it myself.” “It’s okay, don’t worry.” “I don’t want to trouble you.”Being independent is not a problem. But it can become difficult when a person feels they must manage everything alone, even when accepting help would make life easier. Psychologists discuss this partly through the idea of attachment avoidance. People with higher attachment avoidance tend to feel less comfortable with emotional closeness or relying on others. This does not mean every independent person has avoidant attachment. Attachment exists on a spectrum, and one reaction to kindness is not enough to identify someone’s attachment style.A 2022 meta-analysis examined adult attachment and mental health across 224 studies involving 79,722 participants. It found associations between attachment anxiety, attachment avoidance and several mental health outcomes. The research looked at broad patterns, not the reason behind one person’s reaction to affection.They may feel they have to earn loveConsider someone who feels valuable when they are useful. They help their family, complete their work, solve problems and take care of others. Being needed makes them feel important. But when someone shows affection without asking for anything in return, they may feel unsure. A friend says, “You are such a wonderful person.” Their response is: “But what have I done?”This can happen when a person connects their self-worth to achievement, usefulness or other people’s approval. They may find it easier to believe, “I deserve appreciation because I helped someone,” than, “Someone cares about me simply because I am me.”In a 2004 study published in Personality and Social Psychology Bulletin, researchers examined attachment styles and contingencies of self-worth among college students. The study explored how people’s sense of value could be connected to sources such as approval, relationships and achievement. The findings do not prove that everyone who struggles to accept affection has low self-esteem. They suggest that the way people build their sense of worth can influence how they experience positive attention.Compliments may not fit their self-imageSomeone tells you, “You did an excellent job.” You reply, “It was nothing special.” Or: “I just got lucky.” Why dismiss something positive? One possible explanation is that the compliment does not match the way you see yourself. If a person believes they are average, incapable or not particularly talented, praise may feel difficult to accept. Instead of changing their view of themselves, they explain away the compliment.Some people are simply shy. Others do not enjoy being the centre of attention. Some may have grown up in families where openly accepting praise was discouraged. The reaction becomes more interesting when the person feels uncomfortable even with affection from people they trust.Emotional closeness can feel unfamiliarAffection is not limited to hugs or saying “I love you.” It can be a friend asking how you are and genuinely wanting to hear the answer. It can be a partner offering comfort after a difficult day. It can be someone sitting beside you without expecting you to entertain them. For a person who is not used to emotional openness, these moments may feel exposing.Research has examined the relationship between attachment and comfort with physical affection. A 2014 study published in Personality and Individual Differences looked at adults’ feelings about cuddling in romantic and parent-child relationships. It found that attachment avoidance was associated with less positive feelings towards cuddling in both settings.They may be more comfortable giving care than receiving itSome people are excellent at supporting others. But when they need support, they may say, “I’m fine.” Giving care allows them to remain active and in control. Receiving care asks them to pause and allow someone else to take responsibility for a moment. For someone who has spent years being the dependable one, this change can feel strange. It may also involve vulnerability. A 2005 paper by Mario Mikulincer and Phillip Shaver discussed attachment theory and emotions in close relationships. The authors examined how attachment-related patterns can shape reactions to closeness, support and emotional experiences.How to become more comfortable with receiving affectionIf you recognise yourself in this, you do not have to force yourself to accept every form of kindness.Start with a simple thank you: When someone compliments you, try saying, “Thank you. That means a lot.” You do not need to explain why they are wrong.Notice the first feeling: When someone offers help, ask yourself whether you feel guilt, suspicion, embarrassment or fear of being a burden.Accept small acts of care: Let someone make you a cup of tea. Accept help with a small task. Allow a friend to listen when you are having a difficult day.Keep your boundaries: You can appreciate someone’s kindness and still decline a hug, refuse help or ask for space.Speak to a professional if needed: If discomfort with affection repeatedly affects your relationships or leaves you distressed, a mental health professional can help you explore self-worth, trust and emotional closeness.Looking for trusted parenting advice? Follow TOI Parenting Circle on Instagram for expert guidance, relatable stories, and practical tips delivered every day.Get the latest Lifestyle News and more. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Why does Canada want to join the Europe-led JEF military partnership?
articles.summary: This is the latest step in Canada’s bid to move closer to Europe amid bitter trade war with the US.
articles.body:
Canada has applied to join the Joint Expeditionary Force (JEF), a European military coalition, as it seeks to diversify its diplomatic and security ties following a sharp downturn in relations with the United States.

Prime Minister Mark Carney made the request on Wednesday during an official trip to the United Kingdom, which he visited after meeting with European Commission chief Ursula von der Leyen in Brussels. She invited Canada to become the first-ever “associate member” of the bloc.

In a statement, Carney called the UK-led JEF an “important initiative”.

Canada and the US have recently hit each other with tit-for-tat tariffs after trade talks failed. Ottawa has subsequently launched a transatlantic charm offensive to reduce its heavy reliance on the US on everything from trade to defence.

Here’s what we know about the military force and what Canadian membership might mean:

Formed in 2014, the coalition is made up of 10 European states and aims to be capable of rapid military deployments to deter threats from Russia in areas around the North Sea, the wider North Atlantic-Arctic region and the Baltic.

It is led by the UK and has its headquarters in Northwood, just north of London. Denmark, Estonia, Finland, Iceland, Latvia, Lithuania, the Netherlands, Norway and Sweden are its other members.

JEF states, among its conditions for membership: A common strategic interest in the security of Northern Europe, the High North, the North Atlantic, and the Baltic Sea region; shared values, including a belief in democracy, human rights and the rules-based international order; and NATO alignment.

The JEF acts independently of the NATO alliance, although it can support NATO or United Nations missions if needed.

Participation in exercises is voluntary, but members of the JEF should have “political will and trust” as it operates as a “coalition of the willing” rather than with a treaty, the organisation says.

The UK military envisaged it to function as a faster, more adaptable force with less bureaucratic drag. It is designed to take action “below the traditional threshold of war”, according to the UK parliament, meaning it can bypass issues NATO might hesitate to address because of its “an attack on one is an attack on all” policy, which carries a high risk of escalation.

Combined, the JEF’s rapid response forces number about 10,000 soldiers. The alliance has not been deployed yet on any high-stakes missions, so it remains untested.

There are, however, questions about how effective UK leadership might be, as London itself is viewed by MPs as not spending enough on defence at the moment.

A highly critical report by the parliamentary defence committee last year found that the UK is “nowhere near” where it needs to be to defend itself and allies. The report added that the UK is failing to meet its NATO obligations, and falling “far short of its claimed leadership position”.

The UK currently spends about 2.6 percent of its gross domestic product on defence, short of the NATO goal of 3.5 percent by 2035.

UK-based policy think tank, the Royal United Services Institute (RUSI), called for Canada’s inclusion in the JEF last year, and recently urged London to ramp up investment and start deploying the force.

“It has been under-exploited because of the UK’s lack of capacity, so it’s in a position of far less strength than it could be … but changes to the membership structure might see new shifts,” defence analyst Keir Giles, of the Chatham House think tank, told Al Jazeera.

Canada is seeking opportunities that will give the country more options beyond reliance on its traditional ally, the US, amid their ongoing trade war.

Like most other JEF countries, Giles said, Canada has in past decades run down its military forces because of reliance on external forces like the US and NATO, but is now rapidly rebuilding. Although the country’s military capabilities in the NATO alliance are often overlooked because of the US, Giles said Canada has always been a crucial part of NATO’s patrols in the North Atlantic and Baltic waters.

The JEF initially invited Canada to join in 2015, but Ottawa declined, citing the lack of an immediate threat. There are no reports of the US being invited. JEF invitations have so far only been extended to northern Europe and Baltic NATO countries.

But the coalition is concerned with securing areas in the North Atlantic where Canada is a neighbour, meaning there is now some geographical logic to the decision.

Security is only one aspect of the kind of integration Canada is seeking. Canada will likely agree to join the EU as an “associate member”, for example. Besides this, the UK and Canada share Commonwealth ties.

“Canada joining is a logical step because of the JEF’s purpose, because of the cultural affinity it shares with other members and because of a common understanding of how to deal with the threats in that shared area,” Giles noted, adding that the country “now fully understands the dangers of co-dependence with the US”.

Why is Canada having issues with the US?

Canada is locked in a trade war with the US. Back-and-forth retaliatory measures have resulted in both sides slapping new tariffs on each other. That’s especially painful for Canada, which exports 70 percent of all its goods to the US.

In August, trade talks between the two countries broke down, and US President Donald Trump imposed a 50 percent levy on $20bn of Canadian goods, or 5.5 percent of its exports, disrupting the long history of stable relations between the two North American neighbours.

Canada responded with tariffs on US steel, dairy, appliances, farm equipment, pulp and paper, and electronics.

Trump has also previously suggested making Canada a 51st state, raising sovereignty concerns. He appeared to revisit this idea following news that trade talks had broken down when he wrote on his Truth Social platform: “Canada wants the benefits of being a State, without being one!!!” Trump recently renamed Lake Ontario to Lake America in a fit of pique over Ottawa’s refusal to bow down to his demands.

Canada, which has long remained in the shadow of the US in terms of defence, has since launched a strategy to bolster its domestic defence capabilities by ramping up military spending and reducing its reliance on US military suppliers.

Carney’s defence plan, launched earlier this year, will see defence spending increase from about 40 billion Canadian dollars ($28.6bn) to more than 60 billion Canadian dollars ($42.8bn) in the next five years.

This comes as Europe’s relations with Washington have frayed because of tensions over NATO funding. Trump has long claimed that the US shoulders an unfair share of this burden. His insistence on seizing control of Greenland also triggered a standoff.

More recently, European countries’ refusal to be dragged into the US and Israel’s war on Iran has irked the Trump administration.

articles.title: Nithari case victim's father questions Surendra Koli's death, claims murder
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Father of one of the victims in the 2006 Nithari case questioned the death of Surendra Koli in Haridwar on Friday, alleging he was murdered.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Father of one of the victims in the 2006 Nithari case questioned the death of Surendra Koli in Haridwar on Friday, alleging he was murdered and did not die by suicide."Surendra Koli has been murdered; he has not died by suicide", said Jhabbu Lal (64), whose then 15-year-old daughter was among the victims.Koli was found hanging at a rented tea stall on Friday on Sapt Sarovar Road in Haridwar. Police said the scene was examined by a forensic team, with the body's panchanama and post-mortem proceedings under way.Police said the death appeared to be a case of suicide, a claim questioned by Lal."If he had died by suicide in jail, it could be understood that he was depressed. But he took his life after being released and spending several months outside? This raises questions," he said, alleging that Koli could have been killed if he was about to disclose some important case-linked information.He also claimed that Koli was not the main culprit in the Nithari case and accused businessman Moninder Singh Pandher of being one.Koli reportedly worked as a domestic help at Pandher's Noida Sector 31 house."His owner Moninder Pandher was the main accused in the case. He should be hanged," Lal said.Lal and his wife Sunita, 61, have spent nearly 20 years seeking justice for their daughter.According to PTI, the couple hail from Uttar Pradesh’s Unnao district and had moved to Nithari about four decades ago in search of work. Lal made a living by ironing clothes for local residents.“If the government helps us, only then will we be able to continue our fight in future. We can’t fight on our own,” Lal said.The Nithari case came to light in 2006 after skeletal remains, skulls and bones were found in the backyard and drains near Pandher’s D-5 bungalow in Sector 31, Noida.The discovery brought to light the disappearance and killings of several children and young women, sparking nationwide outrage. articles.title: UK, Ireland reaffirm Northern Ireland agreement after Trump remarks spark fresh unification debate
articles.summary: UK News: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham and Irish Taoiseach (prime minister) Micheal Martin on Friday reaffirmed their commitment to upholding the Good Friday .
articles.body: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham and Irish Taoiseach (prime minister) Micheal Martin on Friday reaffirmed their commitment to upholding the Good Friday Agreement, Downing Street said in a statement after the two leaders met in Manchester."The two leaders began by reaffirming the close partnership between the UK and Ireland, as well as their shared commitment to upholding the Good Friday Agreement," Reuters quoted a Downing Street spokeswoman as saying.The statement follows recent comments by US President Donald Trump during his visit last week to Ireland, where he pushed Irish unification onto the political agenda by stating he would "love to see Ireland and Northern Ireland unified."Established in 1998, the Good Friday Agreement ended 30 years of violent conflict between Irish nationalists advocating for a united Ireland and unionists wishing to remain part of the United Kingdom. Under its provisions, a referendum on Irish unification can only be called at the discretion of the British government.Also, on September 14, the first ministers of Northern Ireland, Scotland, and Wales gathered in Welsh capital, Cardiff, where they signed a Memorandum of Understanding declaring that "Westminster's time is up," referring to the UK's Parliament. The three "devolved" nations, and England, make up the United Kingdom.Although the MoU carries no legal binding—as the leaders attended in their political capacities rather than as official state representatives—the agreement is considered landmark as it marks the first time that Northern Ireland, Scotland, and Wales simultaneously have First Ministers who favour leaving the UK or, in Northern Ireland's case, supporting a united Ireland.

articles.title: Chinese ship rams Philippines gov’t vessel in South China Sea: Coastguard
articles.summary: Philippine Coast Guard accuses China of dangerous military manoeuvres near Palawan province.
articles.body:
A Chinese vessel has rammed a Philippine government ship in the South China Sea, according to Manila.

The Philippine Coast Guard on Friday accused a China Coast Guard vessel of carrying out dangerous military manoeuvres before hitting the BRP Datu Magat Salamat off the coast of Palawan province. The collision is the latest in a series of flashpoints between ships from the two nations in the disputed area of the sea.

No injuries were reported in the incident, as debris spilled across the deck of the struck vessel, which belonged to the Philippine government’s Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources (BFAR) and was on a mission to supply fuel to Philippine fishermen.

Coastguard spokesman Jay Tarriela said the Chinese ship initially cut across the path of the Philippine vessel at a distance of about 10 metres (33ft).

Some 10 minutes later, it repeated the manoeuvre and rammed the ship, causing severe damage to one side, added Tarriela, who released video footage allegedly showing the incident.

China rejected the account, placing responsibility for the collision with the Philippine side.

Citing information from the Chinese coastguard, a Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesman said the Philippine vessel had ignored warnings, intentionally altered its course, and suddenly accelerated ahead of the bow of the Chinese ship.

Such incidents have become common in the area, as China seeks to back up its claim to sovereignty over nearly the entirety of the South China Sea.

In July, Manila accused Beijing of firing a water cannon at government vessels near the Scarborough Shoal and hitting a Philippine Navy staff member with a wooden baton in the head.

A month before the altercation, China barred the Philippines’ Minister of National Defence Gilberto Teodoro from entering the country.

Teodoro said in a a statement he would continue protecting Manila “in the face of the wickedness they [China] are committing here and even in our seas”.

Chinese Minister of National Defence Dong Jun has called on other countries to halt “provocative” actions in the sea.

The United States has voiced concern over Beijing’s military activities in the area, as well as criticising a Chinese-designated nature reserve it says is designed to try to reinforce China’s territorial claims.

Manila, a US ally, has continued to push back against Chinese assertiveness in those waters it considers part of its territory.

A United Nations-backed tribunal in July said China’s sovereignty claims have no legal basis.

articles.title: Smooth take off: Pilot handles Punjab turbulence with ‘no CM face’ formula; but can he carry Congress beyond winning line?
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: The Congress in Punjab has finally hit the ground running. Sachin Pilot, who replaced Bhupesh Baghel as the party’s state in-charge, succes.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Congress in Punjab has finally hit the ground running. Sachin Pilot, who replaced Bhupesh Baghel as the party’s state in-charge, successfully navigated the state unit out of months of internal turmoil and ensured the party’s campaign for the 2027 assembly elections could finally take off.With arch-rivals - former chief minister Charanjit Singh Channi and state Congress chief Raja Warring - on board, Pilot led a mega protest demanding the resignation of Punjab finance minister Harpal Cheema, who faces charges of abetment of suicide of a Dalit, Gulzar Singh.The entire state leadership and thousands of party workers marched towards Cheema’s residence. Police used water cannons to stop the protesters’ march. But the point was made. The Congress was finally in action mode.Pilot ensured that Channi and Warring, whose open power tussle has derailed Congress’s Punjab campaign, not only shared the stage but also did a “tense” handshake.Putting up a huge show of unity during the protest, Channi said, "We will fight together." Warring reciprocated. The state Congress chief called Channi and other leaders his 'pagg da lar' (the fold of his turban).Expressing gratitude to party workers for mobilising in such huge numbers at short notice, Pilot assured each one of them that the Congress will always stand by them. The Punjab Congress has seen a no-holds-barred battle between Channi and Warring ever since the high command announced on July 1 that Warring would continue as Punjab Congress chief, ignoring Channi’s claims.The announcement triggered immediate protests from Channi’s supporters. They demanded that Channi should be projected as the party’s CM face in the assembly elections. What followed left the Congress leadership red-faced. From war or words to slogan-shouting at party meetings, the wide split in the state unit was out in the open. The Congress sent Chhattisgarh chief minister Bhupesh Baghel to firefight, but he was also singed in the crossfire. Channi camp leaders accused him of siding with Warring.Pilot, who was then air-dashed to Punjab to set the house in order, has passed his maiden test. But assembly elections in the state are still at least 5 months away. Holding the rival factions together till then will indeed be a daunting challenge for the former Rajasthan deputy chief minister.(function(){function e(){window.addEventListener(`message`,function(e){if(e.data[`datawrapper-height`]!==void 0){var t=document.querySelectorAll(`iframe`);for(var n in e.data[`datawrapper-height`])for(var r=0,i;i=t[r];r++)if(i.contentWindow===e.source){var a=e.data[`datawrapper-height`][n]+`px`;i.style.height=a}}})}e()})();Well begun is half doneSo, how did Pilot cross the first hurdle smoothly? What did he do differently, which Bhupesh Baghel couldn’t?Former Chhattisgarh chief minister Bhupesh Baghel was sent to Punjab in February this year. The Congress in Punjab then was a deeply divided house. Baghel worked hard on the ground to bridge differences between the state leaders. But on July 1, when the Congress high command announced to continue with Raja Warring as the state Congress president and made Channi the head of the campaign committee, the rebellion in the state unit came out in the open.Channi’s supporters openly opposed the decision. But the rebels had lost his trust and refused to budge.With the rebels refusing to relent and their open infighting embarrassing the party leadership, the Congress high command decided to do a course correction to set its house in order.Baghel was shifted out, Pilot was brought in with a clear message: Congress would contest the 2027 assembly elections under collective leadership, and Rahul Gandhi would be the face of the campaign. But at what cost? Congress’s decision to fight the Punjab assembly elections under collective leadership, with Rahul Gandhi as the face of the campaign, may have at best delayed the inevitable power tussle.But it creates another challenge for the party. Much of the Congress’s success in the state till now has been driven by a strong local leadership - Captain Amarinder Singh, who is now with the BJP.The AAP has already announced to contest the upcoming assembly elections under the leadership of Bhagwant Singh Mann. For the Akalis, Sukhbir Singh Badal is the undisputed leader and the party’s campaign revolves around him.That leaves us with the BJP and the Congress.PM Modi vs RahulThe Congress decision to contest Punjab assembly elections with Rahul Gandhi as the party’s face makes the upcoming electoral contest interesting, and perhaps also challenging for the party.The BJP has already launched an aggressive campaign for Punjab with Prime Minister Narendra Modi leading the party’s campaign. PM Modi has already held two rallies in the poll-bound state and has announced a slew of development projects. As the campaign progresses, we will see the Prime Minister go all out against BJP’s political opponents. The BJP, which is in the process of building the party in the state, also has no visible local leadership. It has acquired quite a few prominent leaders from AAP and Congress, but it is unlikely any of them would be projected as the CM face. BJP’s campaigns in states are mostly centralised, with all top leaders campaigning for the party and PM Modi leading the charge. Punjab should be no exception.And that is what should worry the Congress. The fight to conquer Punjab could well become another PM Modi vs Rahul contest. In several such direct contests in the past, the Congress has struggled. However, Punjab could be different. The BJP, for a greater part of its existence in the state, has played second fiddle to the Akalis. The BJP has announced a solo contest in 2027 elections.For the Congress, Punjab has been one of the happiest hunting grounds. articles.title: West Berkshire Council's Grazeley Solar Farm expected to be progressed
articles.summary: The council expects the solar farm to generate enough power every year to power about 5,500 homes.
articles.body:
A £18.6m solar farm that a council wants to build on some of its agricultural land should continue, councillors will be told next week.

West Berkshire Council's Grazeley Solar Farm could produce enough electricity to power at least 5,500 homes, the authority said.

Planning permission has already been granted for the council-owned site at Bloomfield Hatch Farm, between Mortimer and Grazeley, and it expects to make a profit of about £400,000 annually over 30 years.

Senior councillors will be asked to progress the project at a meeting on Thursday, which would allow officers to organise procurement and connections to the grid.

The council has said a contractor is expected to run the farm for its first two years.

Following that, a new contract will be sought for its operation and maintenance, which is expected to cost about £200,000 a year.

The site could still be used for farmland after the solar farm has been removed, the council said. It is classified as low-grade land.

A plan to use the site for housing was shelved previously because of its proximity to the Atomic Weapons Establishment's (AWE) base in Burghfield.

"Grazeley Solar Farm is an important opportunity to make productive use of council-owned land, generate local renewable electricity and support our commitment to tackling the climate and ecological emergency," Stuart Gourley, the council's executive member for environment and highways, said.

"The updated work shows that, while there are risks to manage, the project continues to offer a strong strategic case and the potential to deliver long-term environmental and financial benefits for West Berkshire residents."

articles.title: AI, jobs and voting age on Wakefield pupils' minds
articles.summary: The Children's Commissioner visits Wakefield as part of a nationwide survey of young people.
articles.body:
Artificial intelligence, lowering the voting age and the state of the jobs market have all been debated by schoolchildren in Wakefield as part of a nationwide study.

Dame Rachel de Souza, Children's Commissioner for England, visited Outwood Grange Academy on Thursday as part of the "Big Future" survey she is conducting with one million schoolchildren across the UK.

The survey was set up in response to the government lowering the voting age to 16 ahead of the next general election, with the commissioner saying she wanted to find out young people's "biggest concerns" and "their hopes for the future".

Dame Rachel said children were "not getting what they need in terms of policy".

The 14 and 15-year-olds who spoke to Dame Rachel offered a mixed view on how optimistic they were about their future prospects in life and work.

One student, Celine, told her: "I'm hopeful for the future because I've got a really great education. However, I am worried about climate change."

Meanwhile, Florette said: "I feel quite contradicted, because a lot of students in the UK, once they turn 16, they go to colleges that are further afield.

"A lot of them, their parents can't take them, they have to get public transport.

"If we're expected to do things like that, I think we should have a say in these things.

"However, we're not adults until we're 18. We can't smoke, we can't drink. I wouldn't want children voting.

Florette added: "If we're allowed to vote then people are going to say we should be allowed to do other things [at 16] and it's a slippery slope, I think.

"But I don't completely disagree with it. We should have more voice."

At the event in Wakefield, Gracie told Dame Rachel that she was "quite worried" about the years ahead, "because once I've got my qualifications I'm not sure what I want to do".

She added: "When I try to get a job [I worry] no-one will accept me because I need the work experience, but I can't get the work experience if no-one will accept me."

Jacob said he was "optimistic for the future", but said his ADHD and autism diagnosis "makes me worry about my rights in the workplace".

Last year the government legislated to allow 16-year-olds to vote in the next general election , marking the biggest change in the electorate since the minimum age was dropped from 21 to 18 in 1969.

Dame Rachel said: "We've got a brand new government and they should be taking children seriously. They are not getting what they need in terms of policy and the focus on their lives."

"All this talent and ability in Wakefield needs rocket boosting," she added.

articles.title: Mamata gets 'footballer', but can she win TMC 'khela'? Maharashtra has a red-card warning
articles.summary: India News: For 28 years, TMC has been Mamata Banerjee and Mamata Banerjee has been TMC in West Bengal; the two are almost synonymous with each other. And for vot.
articles.body: For 28 years, TMC has been Mamata Banerjee and Mamata Banerjee has been TMC in West Bengal; the two are almost synonymous with each other. And for voters, the political shorthand for Mamata Banerjee has been almost absurdly simple: two flowers on grass.Now, that shorthand has been taken away.The Election Commission on Friday allotted Mamata's faction a new name - 'Mamata All India Trinamool Congress', with a football player as its symbol. The rival Arup Roy faction will contest as 'Democratic Trinamool Congress', with an 'envelope' as its symbol. The decision follows the commission's September 17 order freezing the original All India Trinamool Congress name and its reserved 'flowers and grass' symbol for the upcoming bypolls.But the EC's interim arrangement is only the first chapter. The substantive question of who gets the original TMC name and symbol will have to be decided under Paragraph 15 of the Election Symbols (Reservation and Allotment) Order, 1968.And here, the story might look familiar.The same movie was played out twice in Maharashtra in recent years, first with the Shiv Sena and then with the Nationalist Congress Party.They do not know that I cannot leave TMC. It will always be with me until I leave this world. Absolutely dirty game, but we are also ready to fight it out. I want the BJP to go from India. We want solidarity in INDIA alliance.What Shiv Sena and NCP cases tell usWhen Shiv Sena split between Uddhav Thackeray and Eknath Shinde in 2022, the EC first froze the party's 'bow and arrow' symbol and allotted separate interim identities to the two factions. In its February 2023 decision, the commission eventually recognised the Shinde faction as the Shiv Sena and allowed it to use the original name and symbol.The NCP followed a similar path. After Ajit Pawar's rebellion in July 2023, the EC decided in February 2024 that the faction led by Sharad Pawar had a weaker numerical claim, while Ajit Pawar's group had superior support in the organisational and legislative wings. It consequently recognised Ajit Pawar's faction as the NCP and allowed it to use the party's 'clock' symbol. The EC order specifically recorded that the Ajit Pawar group had "far superior numerical support" in the organisational and legislative wings.That is a crucial part of the precedent for the ongoing TMC dispute.The conclusion from the Maharashtra cases may be that the EC followed the majority of legislators. The legal position is more nuanced. Paragraph 15 allows the election commission to examine rival claims through the party's organisational structure as well as its legislative strength.In its May 11, 2023 Constitution Bench judgment in Subhash Desai vs Principal Secretary, Governor of Maharashtra, the Supreme Court held that the EC need not determine a party's identity solely through the numerical strength of its MLAs or MPs while adjudicating a dispute under Paragraph 15 of the Symbols Order. The court said the EC could consider the majority in the organisational wing, the party constitution and, where appropriate, "any other appropriate test", underlining that a split among legislators is not necessarily the same as a split in the political party itself.The observation is particularly relevant to the TMC case, where the eventual contest could involve competing claims over the party's organisational structure and not just a headcount of elected representatives. The Supreme Court, however, did not itself decide which faction should receive the Shiv Sena's name and symbol, leaving the merits of that EC decision to separate proceedings.That distinction could matter considerably in the TMC case.The Shiv Sena and NCP rebels who ultimately secured the original party identities had substantial support among sitting legislators. The TMC's internal arithmetic, however, has to be examined on its own terms.The 2026 assembly election setback changed the party's internal arithmetic sharply. Its tally fell from 215 of 294 seats in 2021 to 80, and within weeks, 58 MLAs backed expelled leader Ritabrata Banerjee as their legislature party leader. He was subsequently recognised as leader of the opposition, while the rebel camp rejected Mamata's nominee, Sobhandeb Chattopadhyay.The revolt then spread to Parliament, with 20 Lok Sabha MPs led by Kakoli Ghosh Dastidar joining the NCPI and backing the BJP-led NDA. The TMC challenged their move before the Lok Sabha speaker and sought their disqualification. What began as a post-election leadership challenge had thus expanded into a contest over control of the party's legislative and parliamentary wings.Mamata Banerjee, however, remains the founder and central political figure of the organisation, and her camp's claim is not based only on her position as party leader but also on its organisational and electoral support.The 'new' Mamata partyThe names allotted on Friday were revealing because neither faction chose to abandon the Trinamool identity. Mamata's camp was given 'Mamata All India Trinamool Congress', while the rival Arup Roy camp became 'Democratic Trinamool Congress'. Both were, in different ways, laying claim to continuity with the party Mamata Banerjee founded on January 1, 1998.The distinction lies in the source of legitimacy each side is emphasising. The rebels' use of 'Democratic' fits their argument that the TMC's organisational functioning should be more representative and less centred around one leader. Mamata's faction, meanwhile, has effectively put the founder's name where the old party identity used to be, making 'Mamata' part of its temporary electoral brand. That is particularly striking for a party whose political identity has been inseparable from its founder for almost three decades.They had said beforehand, 'naam bhi rakhne doonga, nishaan bhi nahi rakhne doonga' (Neither let you keep the name nor the symbol). Who are these people? They are in power today; they might not be in power tomorrow. They should understand their limitations.The football-player symbol allotted to Mamata's faction also carries its own political resonance in Bengal. Football has long had a deep cultural presence in the state, but there is also a direct connection to the TMC's campaign vocabulary: 'Khela Hobe', the slogan that became a defining part of Mamata's 2021 assembly campaign against the BJP.The symbol does not automatically recreate that campaign, but it gives the Mamata faction a ready-made visual association at a time when it has lost the party symbol voters have known for nearly three decades.The test, however, has now changed in a rather dramatic way for the Mamata faction.(function(){function e(){window.addEventListener(`message`,function(e){if(e.data[`datawrapper-height`]!==void 0){var t=document.querySelectorAll(`iframe`);for(var n in e.data[`datawrapper-height`])for(var r=0,i;i=t[r];r++)if(i.contentWindow===e.source){var a=e.data[`datawrapper-height`][n]+`px`;i.style.height=a}}})}e()})();Nandigram changes the bypoll testMamata faction's candidate, Sanchita Pradhan Dey, withdrew her nomination from the Nandigram contest altogether, a day before the deadline. Her withdrawal came minutes after she met West Bengal chief minister and BJP leader Suvendu Adhikari, although the circumstances surrounding the meeting and her decision remain a matter of political speculation.Mamata Banerjee later announced in a press conference that her party will now back the Congress candidate in Nandigram, and mentioned that the decision was taken "for the greater interest of the nation" and to strengthen the INDIA bloc."Rahul Gandhi rang me up yesterday, Arvind Kejriwal also expressed solidarity; we will all fight together against BJP. We will support Congress in the Nandigram bypoll to strengthen the INDIA bloc," Mamata said. The Congress candidate, however, was also arrested by the cops late in the evening in a land-grab case.That makes the October 6 bypolls a very different test from the one that appeared possible 24 hours earlier. The Mamata faction will now not be testing its new 'football-player' identity in Nandigram, but instead, ask its supporters to transfer their support to a Congress candidate, even as the rival TMC faction contests the seat under its own new identity.The political significance is difficult to miss. At precisely the moment when the EC has stripped Mamata's faction of the old TMC name and symbol and given it a new identity, the faction is now out of a direct fight in Nandigram, a constituency that carries an unusually strong personal history for both Mamata and Suvendu Adhikari.Nandigram was where Mamata lost to Adhikari in the 2021 assembly election, after making the constituency the centrepiece of her campaign. Adhikari, who had moved from the TMC to the BJP before that election, defeated her by a narrow margin in a contest that became one of the defining episodes of Bengal politics. He subsequently retained Nandigram while also winning Bhowanipore, which he vacated to retain Nandigram, necessitating the October 6 bypoll.The EC may eventually decide who owns the TMC name and symbol, but the October 6 bypolls will offer the first test of how much of the old Trinamool identity survives without 'flowers and grass'. In Rejinagar, the football player and envelope will face each other directly; in Nandigram, Mamata's decision to back Congress will test whether her political support can travel even when her own new party name and symbol are not on the ballot.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Country music star pulled her Bible into bed with her to get through divorce
articles.summary: Karen Waldrup, a country music star based in Nashville, reveals how she channeled the heartbreak of her fall 2025 divorce into powerful new music, including "Keeping the Faith."
articles.body: Accustomed to performing under the bright lights of concert halls as well as TV studios during her time as a finalist on "The Voice," country music star Karen Waldrup of Nashville never anticipated the darkness and despair that would accompany a divorce. But she told Fox News Digital this week in a moving interview how she got through the most "awful" times in the fall of 2025, even while recording new songs, including "Keeping the Faith" and "Just in Case," which is out Friday, Sept. 18. The songs and the phrases have deep resonance with her Christian faith, she said. 105 YEAR-OLD CREDITS THE GOOD LORD FOR HER LONG LIFE: ‘EVERY DAY IS A BLESSING’ "'Keeping the Faith' is one of my favorite songs I've ever been a part of," she said. It's not just about "keeping the faith, it's about keeping the hope, keeping the dream, keeping the focus, keeping the optimism. I went through a really challenging time in the fall of 2025. ... It was awful. So many people know the disheartening horror of that experience, and it was terrible." "But I decided to make a song, ‘Keeping the Faith,'" said the Louisiana-born singer-songwriter. "And the day that I tracked that song was a tough day. It was the toughest day that I've ever been in the studio. And I didn't know if it was even going to come out good because I felt so broken. ‘QUIET QUITTING’ IN MARRIAGE: THE SUBTLE SIGNS A SPOUSE HAS EMOTIONALLY CHECKED OUT "But I think in the end, the song came out great because of the brokenness," she said. "I think you can kind of hear it in the vocal, the desperation of keeping the faith and saying, ‘Hey, you know what, no matter what goes on, you got to get back up and go, you got it. Pick it up. You got to keep the faith.’ And so I'm proud of that song." "It's so heartbreaking. But after you come out of it, I truly believe that you are stronger." Waldrup was not only a top 5 finalist on Season 25 of "The Voice," she’s a BMI songwriter and a member of the Recording Academy (NARAS) and the Country Music Association (CMA). She's won 12 Nashville Industry Music Awards and has seven studio albums and over 50 songs released worldwide. "After a lot of time, reflection and prayer, I’m ready to share that my marriage has ended in divorce," she wrote to fans in February on her Facebook page. "This has been a deeply personal journey, and I’ve taken the time I needed to process it privately. I’m grateful for the love, grace and support around me, and I appreciate kindness as I continue to move forward." She told Fox News Digital, "There's a bridge [in the song ‘Keeping the Faith’] that says, 'There's a reason I'm still standing here stronger than I ever knew.' "And I think after you go through something like that, your whole dream of a lifelong marriage goes away and is no longer a part of your life — it's so heartbreaking," she went on. "But after you come out of it, I truly believe that you are stronger. People are stronger from this experience. "My faith definitely carried me through that season, the fall of 2025. I was very vulnerable," she said. "I had to keep going. … My faith was the foundation of what got me through that." "We were working on the record, and I had to keep going. I look at people like Dolly Parton or Reba [McEntire], and I think about how many times they had somebody pass away, and they had to get back up on stage — or they had their mom in the hospital or something, and they had to go play a show," she added. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS "And when I was going through that, I was actually sleeping with my Bible every single night, in the bed with me at night. I was waking up every morning, opening my scripture and reading it. My faith was definitely the foundation of what got me through that." She said her friends made a difference as well. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER "My friends believed in me. They believed I would get through it. They never doubted me. And one of the things I did, I made a list of the top six people — one being God, so God plus five people — that I felt like I could really talk to about what I was going through without them making me feel worse." "And I tried to really only talk to those five people," said Waldrup. "Sometimes when you're going through something like a divorce, everyone has their opinions. Everyone has all these different things that people want to say. And so I found that was a really helpful thing. "When you're going through something tough in life, rather than listening to the opinions of 50 people, you can kind of go, OK, these are the five people that, when I talk to this person, make me feel like I'm gonna get through this. And those are the people that I really leaned on. So my faith, my scripture and my friends." TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ Waldrup said she believes she is "living God's purpose for my life." "I do think part of my purpose in music is to inspire. I don't make my musical experience all about me," she said. "This music is a gift, this show is a gift, this moment is a gift." "My friends believed in me. They believed I would get through it." And "I believe in giving," she added. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "I don't really need to be important. All I need to do is do God's work. … He gave me this voice. And we're talking about faith, we're talking about music, we're talking about joy, we're talking about friendship, and about love — or the lack thereof. "There are so many things that we are called to talk about in life. And I do feel like I'm living God's purpose for my life." Waldrup has performed in more than 15 countries. Her newest single "Just in Case" is available now.

articles.title: Unheard Oasis recordings valued at £1.6m set for Evesham auction
articles.summary: The hidden tapes have been in the possession of a former sound engineer's family for 20 years.
articles.body:
Oasis fans are set for a Wonderwall experience when they get the chance to bid for unheard recordings of the Supersonic boys at their peak.

The archive includes recordings of 63 live shows, soundchecks and more than 100 hours of rehearsals from the band's rise and rise in the 1990s that have been valued at between £1.2m and £1.6m.

The lots, which also include original setlists, tour itineraries, a band-played Epiphone guitar and an Oasis tour parka, will be offered for sale on 3 October in Evesham, Worcestershire.

The collection, known as The Desk Tapes, has been in the possession of Owain Richards for 20 years, after his dad, a former front-of-house sound engineer joined the band's crew during their heyday.

"Dad labelled everything, recorded everything and backed it all up to cassette, over and over," he said.

"I grew up listening to these recordings. Oasis were part of the family as much as they were part of the culture."

Littleton Auctions is handling sale and say the tapes, recorded directly from the sound desk, form the only master archive of their kind.

Also among the items due to go under the hammer is a pair of Adidas Kegler Super Ostrich trainers gifted to Noel Gallagher.

Only 100 pairs were produced in 2000 to mark the 100th anniversary of Adidas founder Adi Dassler.

Ben Homer, managing director of Littleton Auctions, described it as "one of the most exciting collections" the auction house had brought to market.

The sale will take place online and in person with bidders, who are required to register in advance and pay a deposit, hoping they won't be looking back in anger on the day.
